name: Astra AI
tagline: Subscription AI assistant: chat, writing help and a grab bag of model-powered tools behind one login.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: This is an assistant layer sitting on top of models it does not own, reached through a paid search ad. The product surface is a chat window, some saved prompts, maybe file upload and image generation, all of which a coding agent can assemble in an evening against an API key you already have. What you are actually paying for is the packaging and the inference bill, not any capability that is locked up. If you use it heavily every day the metered API cost can exceed a flat subscription, so run the numbers before you feel smug. If you use it a few times a week, a local build plus pay-per-token is cheaper and your history stays on your machine.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app with streaming chat against an OpenAI-compatible API, saved prompt presets, file and image attachments, and conversation history in SQLite.
requirements: An API key for at least one model provider
Willingness to pay per token instead of a flat fee
whatYouLose: Native mobile and tablet apps with push, share sheets and voice input
A flat monthly price that hides token spend and never surprises you
Whatever proprietary prompt library, templates or tuned defaults ship in the product
Localized UI and support in Spanish and other languages
Sync across devices without you standing up hosting and auth
moatNotes: The real distribution advantage here is ad budget on branded keywords, which is not a moat you can copy or need to.
whyPeopleStillPay: Most buyers of an assistant like this are not going to create a provider account, guard an API key and reason about token pricing. They want one login, an app icon on the phone, an interface in their own language and a bill they can predict. That convenience is genuinely worth money to a lot of people. It is worth much less to anyone who already has a key in a .env file and is comfortable running a local server.
notes: Any assistant that is a UI over someone else's model is a one-sitting build; the only question is whether you would rather pay per token or per month.
prompt:
Build a local, single-user AI assistant web app. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- Next.js 15 App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind, shadcn/ui
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/assistant.db, schema created on first boot
- Vercel AI SDK for streaming, provider set to any OpenAI-compatible endpoint
- Secrets in .env.local: API_BASE_URL, API_KEY, DEFAULT_MODEL. Never hardcode keys.

In scope:
- Two pane layout: conversation list on the left, chat on the right
- Streaming token-by-token responses, stop button, regenerate last reply, edit-and-resend a user message
- Persist conversations and messages to SQLite, auto-title a conversation from the first user message
- Model picker populated from a MODELS list in a single config file
- Prompt presets: a JSON file of named system prompts (translate, rewrite, summarize, code review, explain like I am five), selectable per conversation and editable in the UI
- Attachments: paste or upload text, markdown, PDF and images. Extract PDF text server side with pdf-parse, send images as base64 to vision-capable models
- Full text search over stored messages using SQLite FTS5
- Export a conversation to markdown, delete a conversation, wipe all data
- Keyboard shortcuts: cmd+k for search, cmd+enter to send, cmd+shift+n for new chat
- Rough per-conversation token and cost estimate from a hardcoded price table in the config file

Out of scope, do not build: user auth, multi-tenancy, payments, a mobile app, RAG over a document library, agent tool calling, analytics.

Deliver: npm install then npm run dev works with only .env.local filled in. Include a README with setup, where the database lives, and how to add a model. Handle API errors and rate limits with a visible inline error, not a silent failure.
